Problem 1. (10 points)A biased coin is tossed repeatedly. The probability of heads is p∈ (0, 1).
Assume all tosses are independent of each other.
Let Y be the (random) time of the ﬁrst appearance of two consecutive heads. That is,
Y := min{n≥ 2 : the outcomes at times n− 1 and n are both heads}.
Here by convention, we assign Y =∞ if there is no n≥ 2 so that the outcomes at times n−

Problem 2. (10 points) Rachel has two coins and a dice. The dice is standard, whereas the coins
are biased: the ﬁrst coin comes out heads with probability p (and comes out tails otherwise) while the
second one comes out heads with probability q (and comes out tails otherwise), where p,q ∈ [0, 1] are
parameters. Rachel is playing the following game. At each turn she tosses the ﬁrst coin. If it comes
out heads she tosses the second coin, otherwise she rolls the dice. The score of the turn is the ﬁnal
result obtained, with score of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 for the faces of the dice and 0 or 1 for the sides of the coin (0
for tails and 1 for heads). Let Xn be the score of the n-th turn, and let Sn =X1 +... +Xn be the total
score achieved in the ﬁrst n turns,n∈ N.

Let A be the event “the classiﬁer ﬂags the email as spam”.
